title: Observability for mobile apps
summary: You cannot attach a debugger to a user's phone. Combine crash reporting, MetricKit performance data, structured logs, client-side traces and business funnels, all privacy-safe and sampled.
requirements: Detect regressions within hours of a release; diagnose without user reports.
No PII in telemetry; bounded battery and data cost.
components: Crash reporter (signal + exception handlers, symbolication with dSYMs)
MetricKit: launch time, hangs, hitches, memory, disk writes, CPU exceptions, diagnostics
Structured logging (`os.Logger` locally; sampled upload of error-level events)
Client tracing: spans for screen load, network, DB; correlated with backend trace IDs via headers
Dashboards and alerts per release and per feature
tradeoffs: Verbose logging helps debugging but costs battery, storage, data and privacy risk; use levels, sampling and on-demand upload.
Third-party SDKs are fast to adopt but add launch time, size and data-sharing concerns; in-house gives control at engineering cost.
body: **Key metrics:** crash-free users/sessions, hang rate, launch p50/p90, scroll hitch rate, screen time-to-interactive, API error rate and latency by endpoint, OOM rate, app size.
**Time to interactive:** start a span on navigation intent, end when the first meaningful content renders; tag with network type and device class.
**Remote debug logging:** a flag enables verbose logging for a specific user (with consent) for 24h to investigate issues.
**Privacy:** hash or drop identifiers, redact URLs and free text, declare collection in the privacy manifest, honor opt-outs.

code.caption: Structured, privacy-aware logging
code.text:
import os
let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.app", category: "checkout")

log.info("Payment started for order \(orderID, privacy: .private(mask: .hash))")
log.error("Payment failed: \(error.code, privacy: .public)")
